paragraphs: FT EARING this excellent speech of that ascetic of immeasurable energy, that foremost of men answered him in these happy words, — “O best of ascetics, I have heard that the Yaksha race is endowed with but small prowess. How bAlakXndam. can then that one of the weaker sex possess the strength of a thousand elephants Y* Hearing this speech that was uttered by Raghava of immeasurable energy, Vi^wSmitra, delighting with his amiable words that subduer of foes, Rama, and Lakshmana, said, — “Do thou listen as to the means whereby attaining terrible strength, that one belonging to the weaker sex hath come to possess strength and prowess by virtue of a boon. In former times there was a mighty and exceedingly powerful Yaksha, named Suketu.

And he had no issue. And he was of pure practices, and used to perform rigid austerities. And, O R&ma, the Grand-sire, well pleased with that lord of Yakshas, conferred upon him a gem of a daughter, by name TarakS. And the Grand-sire endowed her with the strength of a thousand elephants ; yet that illustrious one did not bestow a son on that Yaksha. And when she had grown, and attained youth and beauty, he gave that famous damsel unto Jambha's son, Sunda, for wife. And after a length of time, that Yakshi gave birth to a son, named Maricha, possessed of irrepressible energy — him who became a Rakshasa in consequence of a curse. And, O Rama, when Sunda had been destroyed, T&raka along wit|i her son, set her heart upon afflicting that excellent saint Agastya.

And enraged with Agastya, she rushed at him with a roar, intending to devour him. And on seeing her thus rushing, that worshipful saint, Agastya, said unto Maricha, “Do thou become a Rakshasa !*', and, in exceeding wrath, he also cursed Tarak§. “And, O mighty Yakshi, since in frightful guise with a frightful face thou hast desired to eat up a human being, do thou immediately leave this (thy original) shape, and become of a terrible form ! ” Thus cursed by Agastya, TarakS, overwhelmed with rage, lays waste this fair region, where Agastya carrieth on his austerities. Do thou, O descendant of Raghu, for the welfare of Br&hmanas and kine, slay this exceedingly terrible Yakshi of wicked ways and vile prowess!

Nor, O son of RJlMIYANA. Raghu, doth any one in the three worlds, save, thee, dare to slay this Yakshi joined with a curse. Nor shouldst thou, O best of men, shrink from slaying a woman ; for even this should be accomplished by a prince in the interests of the four orders. And whether an act be cruel or otherwise, slightly or highly sinful, it should for protecting the subjects, be performed by a ruler. Of those engaged in the onerous task of government, even this is the eternal rule of conduct. Do thou, O Kukutstha, slay this impious one; for she knoweth no righteousness ! We hear, O king, that in days of yore, Sakra slew Virochana’s daughter, Manthar5, who had intented to distroy the earth.

And formerly, O Rama, Vishnu destroyed K&vya's mother, the devoted wife of Bhrigu, who had set her heart upon making the world, devoid of Indra. By these as well as innumerable princes — foremost of men — have wicked women been slain. Therefore, O king, renouncing antipathy, do thou, by my command, slay this one! ,,

verses.sa:
अथ तस्याप्रमेयस्य  मुनेर्वचनमुत्तमम्।
श्रुत्वा पुरुषशार्दूलः प्रत्युवाच शुभां गिरम् ॥

अल्पवीर्या यदा यक्षी श्रूयते मुनिपुङ्गव ।
कथं नागसहस्रस्य धारयत्यबला बलम् ॥

इत्युक्तं वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवस्यामितौजसः ।
हर्षयञ्श्लक्ष्णया वाचा सलक्ष्मणमरिन्दमम् ॥

विश्वामित्रोऽब्रवीद् वाक्यं शृणु येन बलोत्कटा ।
वरदानकृतं वीर्यं धारयत्यबला बलम् ॥

पूर्वमासीन्महायक्षः सुकेतुर्नाम वीर्यवान् ।
अनपत्यः शुभाचारः स च तेपे महत्तपः ॥

पितामहस्तु सुप्रीतस्तस्य यक्षपतेस्तदा ।
कन्यारत्नं ददौ राम ताटकां नाम नामतः ॥

ददौ नागसहस्रस्य बलं चास्याः पितामहः ।
न त्वेव पुत्रं यक्षाय ददौ चासौ महायशाः ॥

तां तु बालां विवर्धन्तीं रूपयौवनशालिनीम् ।
जम्भपुत्राय सुन्दाय ददौ भार्यां यशस्विनीम् ॥

कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य यक्षी पुत्रं व्यजायत ।
मारीचं नाम दुर्धर्षं यः शापाद् राक्षसोऽभवत् ॥

सुन्दे तु निहते राम अगस्त्यमृषिसत्तमम् ।
ताटका सहपुत्रेण प्रधर्षयितुमिच्छति ॥

भक्षार्थं जातसंरम्भा गर्जन्ती साभ्यधावत ।
आपतन्तीं तु तां दृष्ट्वा अगस्त्यो भगवानृषिः ॥

राक्षसत्वं भजस्वेति मारीचं व्याजहार सः ।
अगस्त्यः परमामर्षस्ताटकामपि शप्तवान् ॥

पुरुषादी महायक्षी विकृता विकृतानना ।
इदं रूपम् विहायाशु दारुणं रूपमस्तु ते ॥

सैषा शापकृतामर्षा ताटका क्रोधमूर्छिता ।
देशमुत्सादयत्येनमगस्त्याचरितं शुभम् ॥

एनां राघव दुर्वृत्तां यक्षीं परमदारुणाम् ।
गोब्राह्मणहितार्थाय जहि दुष्टपराक्रमाम् ॥

नह्येनां शापसंसृष्टां कश्चिदुत्सहते पुमान् ।
निहन्तुं त्रिषु लोकेषु त्वामृते रघुनन्दन ॥

नहि ते स्त्रीवधकृते घृणा कार्या नरोत्तम ।
चातुर्वर्ण्यहितार्थं कर्तव्यं राजसूनुना ॥

नृशंसमनृशंसं वा प्रजारक्षणकारणात् ।
पातकं वा सदोषं वा कर्तव्यं रक्षता सदा ॥

राज्यभारनियुक्तानामेष धर्मः सनातनः ।
अधर्म्यां जहि काकुत्स्थ धर्मो ह्यस्यां न विद्यते ॥

श्रूयते हि पुरा शक्रो विरोचनसुतां नृप ।
पृथिवीं हन्तुमिच्छन्तीं मन्थरामभ्यसूदयत् ॥

विष्णुना च पुरा राम भृगुपत्नी पतिव्रता ।
अनिन्द्रं लोकमिच्छन्ती काव्यमाता निषूदिता ॥

एतैश्चान्यैश्च बहुभी राजपुत्रैर्महात्मभिः ।
अधर्मसहिता नार्यो हताः पुरुषसत्तमैः ।
तस्मादेनां घृणां त्यक्त्वा जहि मच्छासनान्नृप ॥
